criteria: Code4rena severity criteria as reproduced in CLAUDE.md, subordinate to the Three-Law hierarchy. High: assets stolen/lost/compromised directly or via a valid attack path with no hypotheticals. Medium: assets not at direct risk, but protocol function/availability impacted, or value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements. QA/Low: state handling, spec deviation, centralization.
gradingStance: The script-auditor's `low` severityHint was treated as a prior to be tested, not accepted. Each finding was graded against demonstrated impact at HEAD b9391b1 and against live chain state at block 25678182. One finding moved OFF the hint (PR24-06 low -> medium, flagged borderline); six were independently re-derived as Low and confirmed; the split leg was graded QA, below the hint. No severity discount was applied for 'it is only a script': this suite performs a mainnet cutover over live user stake, so a defect that mis-executes it carries contract-grade consequences. Equally, no inflation was applied for the same reason - four of the seven have empirically-empty harmful legs (three independent zero reads on chain) and are graded on what they are today, with escalation triggers recorded rather than pre-emptively priced in.

findings.title: Story 076 Concerns §4 states both deposit views are bound to PhlimboV2; the ViewRouter-registered `DepositPageView` is in fact bound to PhlimboV1, so the recorded follow-up would move the live UI onto a staler view

findings.description: Story 076 Concerns §4 declares the view layer out of scope on the stated premise that "both views are bound to V2, and the live deposit UI is on the deprecated one", and records two follow-ups on that basis: (a) redeploy `DepositPageView` against V3, (b) move phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution "the way the mint page already is". The premise is wrong for the router-registered surface. Read live at block 25678182: `ViewRouter(0xC17Ce1cE...).pages(keccak256("deposit"))` resolves to `DepositPageView 0x50D4443782bB9A6e8D65dAcd593684EDd3FF03b8`, whose immutable `phlimbo()` reads `0x3984eBC84d45a889dDAc595d13dc0aC2E54819F4` — PhlimboV1, not PhlimboV2 `0x6084a02C...`. Only the deprecated `DepositView 0x0725722b...` was redeployed against V2 (`mainnet-addresses.ts:12`, story 049 follow-up); `DepositPageView` was left on V1. So the ViewRouter deposit page is already one generation stale TODAY, pre-cutover, and will be two generations stale after Phase 4e.
findings.impact: Two consequences the story's out-of-scope decision did not price in. First, follow-up (b) as written is actively harmful ordering: moving phlimbo-ui's deposit page onto ViewRouter resolution before follow-up (a) lands would migrate users from a V2-correct view onto a V1-stale one, so the recommended sequencing must be (a) then (b), not either order. Second, post-cutover the deprecated `DepositView` the live UI actually reads points at a PhlimboV2 the cutover has deliberately emptied to `totalStaked == 0`, so every migrated user's deposit page reads a zero balance while their principal sits in PhlimboV3. That is a user-visible zero-balance display across the entire migrated user base for as long as the redeploy is outstanding. No asset is at risk — this is a display and operational-sequencing issue, and the redeploy itself is legitimately out of scope for a script-and-tooling story.

classification.likelihood: Leg 3 is certain (it is the designed cutover, not a contingency). Leg 4 is a live operational hazard whose probability is governed only by which follow-up an operator picks up first, with no artifact anywhere telling them the order matters - and the one artifact that discusses it (story 076 Concerns S4) states a premise that makes (b)-first look safe.
classification.assumptions: Assumes story 072 broadcasts (i.e. the cutover this suite exists to perform actually runs). Assumes the DepositPageView redeploy remains outstanding at that moment, which is the current state of record - both follow-ups are unnumbered comments, not scheduled stories. No assumption about operator competence or malice is made; the hazard is that the written record is wrong.
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond the cutover itself. No attacker, no market condition, no third-party contract behaviour.
classification.whyNotHigh: No asset can be stolen, lost or locked. Balances are wrong on a display surface, not in accounting; withdrawals, migration and every value-bearing path are unaffected. There is no attack path of any kind. High would be gross overstatement.
classification.whyNotLow: Low would price this as the stale-pointer fact alone. It is not: the exclusion that let it through is premised on a verified-false statement, the post-cutover wrong-balance display is certain and universal rather than contingent, and the documented fix is inverted with the correcting ordering recorded nowhere. Grading it Low would bury an ordering trap that is live the moment story 072 broadcasts.
classification.borderlineNote: FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW as a deliberate Low->Medium move. The honest counter-case for Low: the harm is a display defect, the remedy is a routine view redeploy, and the V1 staleness has existed since story 049 without reported harm. The case for Medium that I acted on: certainty + universal user scope + a scope exclusion resting on a false premise + an inverted documented remediation with unrecorded ordering. A human who weighs the display-only ceiling more heavily than the ordering trap may reasonably re-grade this Low; the ordering guidance ((a) before (b)) must survive that re-grade either way.

findings.justification: MEDIUM on protocol-function grounds, explicitly NOT on asset grounds. C4 Medium is 'assets not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. Three things weighed together clear that bar where any one alone would not: (a) an on-chain first-party read surface the protocol publishes (ViewRouter's registered deposit page) already serves two-generation-stale state and will serve it about a contract the cutover deliberately empties - guaranteed, universal, and user-visible; (b) the documented scope exclusion that waived this rests on a premise verified false on chain, so the decision to accept it was never actually made against the real facts; (c) the recorded remediation, executed as written, makes the live surface worse rather than better, and the corrective ordering exists in no artifact. Leg (c) is a textbook Law-3 footgun: a competent, non-malicious owner following their own written follow-ups would be surprised to find they had regressed the deposit page a generation. Availability of correct protocol state to every migrated user is impacted; that is Medium.

findings.description: The suite now carries three write-once baselines. Two are mechanically protected against a hand-trimmed progress file: `bptAtCutover` (story 074) and `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover`, whose Phase 0 has an explicit `require(!_isConfigured("p4e_migrate") || phlimboBaselineFromProgressFile, "RESUME ABORT: ...")` at :798-801, precisely because re-deriving it from an emptied V2 would make the conservation assertion vacuous. The third — `phusdMinterMask` / `phusdMintVersion`, which story 076 promoted from a supporting record to the load-bearing input of the two-sided delta — has no such guard. `_snapshotPhusdMinterSet` (:974-997) returns early only when `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile` is already true; otherwise it records the LIVE mask unconditionally, with no reference to whether `p4e_v3_mintGrant` / `p4e_v2_mintRevoke` have already run. A `:resume` whose progress file lost the `baselines` block therefore stamps a post-cutover mask as the Phase 0 baseline and writes it straight back out; `VerifyPromotionReady._verifyMintAuthorityInvariance` then sees `phusdMinterBaselineFromProgressFile == true` (:230-233 satisfied), compares live against a baseline taken from the same post-cutover state, and passes `liveMask == baseline & ~v2Bit` trivially — bit 19 is already clear on both sides after the revoke.
findings.impact: A green `promotion-ready:verify` that proves nothing about the phUSD mint-authority delta — the single control story 076 added to replace story 072's now-false 'minter set byte-identical' invariant, and the one the operator is told (`:232`) is verified NOWHERE ELSE. It fails open, not closed. Reaching it requires an operator hand-trim error on the resume path, which the docs warn against in prose (`:800`, `:171-173`) — but the identical risk on the two sibling baselines was considered serious enough to guard in code, so the asymmetry is the defect.
findings.evidence: side-effects.json.assertionCoverage.baselineGuards — a three-way comparison of the guards on `bptAtCutover`, `phlimboV2StakedAtCutover` (:798-801 deploy-side abort + :190-200 verifier abort) and `phusdMinterMask` (verifier abort at :230-233 only, no deploy-side abort). findings.description: Story 076 Concerns §3 and the inline comment at :1785-1790 argue the V2 mint revoke is safe because two facts hold at the moment it executes: `totalStaked == 0` (so `PhlimboV2._claimRewards` early-returns before its BARE, REVERTING `phUSD.mint` at PhlimboV2.sol:495) and `desiredAPYBps == 0` (so a late staker accrues nothing). Both are enforced by statements that forge evaluates during its single LOCAL execution pass, before transaction #1 is dispatched (the ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast property established by run-23 and documented for this suite in the `:verify` npm doc key). Under `--slow --ledger` the actual broadcast runs for minutes across many blocks, and `PhlimboV2.stake` is ungated and — by this story's own deliberate design — unpausable. findings.impact: A user who stakes into PhlimboV2 during the broadcast window, after Phase 4e's last `migrate` transaction and while V2 still carries a non-zero APY, accrues pending phUSD that V2 can no longer mint once the revoke lands, and their `withdraw` reverts — freezing principal, which is precisely the failure the gate is documented as preventing. findings.recommendation: Two options, both cheap. findings.title: Phase 0 never establishes that PhlimboV2 can mint phUSD during the migration, yet every migrated position with pending phUSD routes through V2's bare, reverting `phUSD.mint`

findings.description: `MigratorV2V3.migrateOne` migrates a user by calling `phlimboV2.withdraw(amount, user)`, which runs `PhlimboV2._claimRewards` (:486) and pays the phUSD leg with a BARE, reverting `phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount)` (:495) whenever `pendingPhUSDAmount > 0`. V3's non-reverting `try`/bank was added by phlimbo story 029 to V3 ONLY. So the migration's per-user body silently depends on PhlimboV2 holding an active phUSD mint grant for any position carrying pending phUSD. Phase 0 reads that grant and LOGS it (:784-787, `console.log("  V2 holds phUSD mint:  ", ...)`) but never requires it, and Phase 4e's step 14 only ever revokes it. Because `migrateOne` runs inside `migrate`'s try/catch, a revert here is absorbed into `UserMigrationSkipped` and the cursor advances — so the failure is a silent skip, not an error, and the hard `require(v2.totalStaked() == 0)` gate at :1779 then aborts the ENTIRE promotion-ready cutover on behalf of a defect three contracts away.

findings.title: PhlimboV3's committed APY is proven only inside the `_isConfigured` gate a resume skips; neither Phase 7 nor VerifyPromotionReady ever reads `v3.desiredAPYBps()` or `v3.apySetInProgress()`

findings.description: Story 076 Autonomous Decision 2 correctly identifies that `desiredAPYBps() == bps` is a vacuous read-back when `bps == 0` (both real cases here), and adds `require(!p.apySetInProgress())` at :1826-1832 so a missed 100-block commit window fails loudly. That non-vacuous proof lives entirely inside `_setDesiredAPYTwoStep`, which Phase 4e calls only from within `if (!_isConfigured("p4e_v3_apy"))` (:1684-1688). `_trackConfig("p4e_v3_apy")` is stamped into the progress file during forge's LOCAL pass (`_trackConfig` -> `_writeProgressFileWithStatus`, :3009-3015), i.e. BEFORE either `setDesiredAPY` transaction is dispatched. If the second (commit) transaction is rejected or dropped on the Ledger, the progress file already records the step as done, a `:resume` skips it, and PhlimboV3 is left latched mid-preview with the APY uncommitted. Grep over both script files confirms `v3.desiredAPYBps()` appears nowhere in Phase 7 or `VerifyPromotionReady` (:2419 checks V2 only), and `apySetInProgress()` appears nowhere outside `_setDesiredAPYTwoStep`. Phase 8's `_probePhlimboV3StakeClaim` cannot substitute: it is preview-only AND it deliberately ARMS its own 1000-bps probe APY whenever it reads 0 (:2530-2535), so it masks exactly this failure.
findings.impact: Today the mirrored target is 0 (verified live: `PhlimboV2.desiredAPYBps() == 0`), so a missed commit leaves V3 at 0 — the same value it was going to be set to, and the impact is confined to a stuck `apySetInProgress` latch.
